editorial:
You follow a young Han Solo as he escapes his rough life on Corellia and stumbles into a crew of smugglers and thieves. Along the way, you meet Chewbacca, Lando, and a crew of colorful characters who pull off heists in a galaxy far, far away. The movie has a fun, adventurous vibe that feels like a classic heist film mixed with Star Wars action. It moves quickly and never takes itself too seriously, which makes it easy to enjoy even if you are not a hardcore fan.

The action scenes are exciting, especially the train heist and the famous Kessel Run. Alden Ehrenreich does a solid job as Han, and Donald Glover steals every scene as Lando. The pacing is fast and the humor lands well. On the downside, the story can feel a bit predictable and some characters do not get enough screen time. If you love Star Wars or just want a fun adventure, you should definitely check it out. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your collection.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Han wins the Millennium Falcon from Lando in a card game and heads off to Tatooine to find a job with Jabba the Hutt. The big twist reveals that Qi'ra, Han's old love, is actually working for the crime syndicate Crimson Dawn and reports to Darth Maul, who appears in a hologram. Han does not know this, so he flies away happy while you are left knowing danger is still close. It sets up a darker future for the characters.
